summary: Rajendralal Mitra was an indologist, historian, archaeologist, and linguist who studied at Hindu School (~1837–1839) and the University of Calcutta. He served as president of the Asiatic Society around 1885.

Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay worked in history, archaeology, and indology. Educated at Presidency University (~1903–1907) and the University of Calcutta (~1907–1910), he held posts at Presidency University, the University of Calcutta (~1908–1911), and Banaras Hindu University (~1928–1930).

Tibetologist Ralf Kramer studied under David P. Jackson, earning an MA from the University of Hamburg by 1997, and studied at the University of London. Around 2004, he was Aris Librarian for Tibetan & Himalayan Studies at Bodleian Libraries.

Ralph Abraham was a philosopher who studied at the University of Michigan (~1956–1960) and under Debabrata SenSharma. He held academic posts at UC Berkeley (~1960–1962), Columbia University (~1962–1964), and UC Santa Cruz (~1968–1994).

Ralph Lilley Turner was an indologist and linguist educated at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1906–1910). He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1915–1922), as Professor at the University of London (~1922–1957), and as Director of SOAS (~1937–1957).

Indologist Ralph T. H. Griffith studied at The Queen's College (~1843–1849) under Horace Hayman Wilson (~1845–1849). He succeeded James R. Ballantyne, serving as Principal of Benares Sanskrit College (~1861–1876).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma studied at Patna University (until ~1953) and completed a PhD under Murray Barnson Emeneau at UC Berkeley (~1956–1959). He held positions at the Central Sanskrit Board and Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University.
Active in religious studies, philosophy, and indology, Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj and established Presidency University, Kolkata, in 1816.

Ram Niwas Pandey, an indologist and historian-archaeologist, studied at Pt. Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha. He held a post at Tribhuvan University.
Ram Shankar Tripathi was a scholar in Buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy. He held professorships at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Historian, archaeologist, and indologist Ram Sharan Sharma studied at Patna College, Patna University (~1937–1943), and SOAS (~1953–1956). He held posts at Patna College (~1943–1973), SOAS (~1964–1965), University of Toronto (~1965–1966), and University of Delhi (~1973–1985).
Rama Nath Sharma is a linguist and indologist who served as a Professor at the University of Rochester (~1968–1976) and at the University of Hawaii (~1976).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an indologist and archaeologist who studied at Dhaka Collegiate School, Dhaka College, and Scottish Church College. He worked at Hindu School, Rajshahi Collegiate School, University of Calcutta, and the Indian Museum (1921–1931).
Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji studied at the University of Calcutta from ~1946 to 1953 and later held an academic post there from ~1957 to 1970.
Ramchandra B. Athavale was an indologist who held positions as Professor of Sanskrit at L. D. Arts College and at Gujarat Vidyapith.

Indologist Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar studied at the University of Mumbai (~1927–1933) and Heidelberg University (~1936–1938). He held posts at Fergusson College (~1933–1950), Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (1950), and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1950–1968).

Indologist and historian Ramesh Chandra Majumdar studied at Hooghly Collegiate School, Surendranath College, Presidency University, Ravenshaw University, and the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Calcutta, the History of Bengal Publication Committee, and University of Chicago.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte worked in indology, history, and archaeology. He was Department Head at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University and a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.
Ramin Etesami is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College (~2013–2015), supervised by Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina.

Ramkrishna Gopal Bhandarkar studied at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai, and University of Göttingen, studying under Martin Haug. An indologist and linguist, he held professorships at Elphinstone College (~1868–1881) and Deccan College (1882), succeeding Franz Kielhorn.
